messages.content: "Could you tell me the estimated date of the Jurassic geological era and calculate how many years ago it was? Also, could you provide the date of the signing of the Magna Carta and calculate how many years ago that event took place?"

function.name: geology_get_era
function.description: Get the estimated date of a geological era. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

era_name.description: The name of the geological era. e.g Ice age

calculate_years_ago.description: True if years ago is to be calculated. False by default

function.name: history_get_event_date
function.description: Get the date of an historical event. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

calculate_years_ago.description: True if years ago is to be calculated. False by default

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

1) Estimated date (start or end?) of the Jurassic geological era. Likely they want start year maybe approximate range. They also ask "calculate how many years ago it was". So we need to compute difference between current year (assuming present day 2026) and some reference point like beginning of Jurassic (~201 million years ago). But likely they'd expect answer like "Jurassic period began about 201 million years ago." That would already include years ago.

But they specifically say "estimated date ... and calculate how many years ago it was". Could interpret as give the time span (e.g., 199–145 Ma), then compute years ago relative to now. For example, starting at ~201 Ma -> 201 million years ago; ending at ~145 Ma -> 145 million years ago. Provide both.

We can use the geology_get_era tool with era_name="Jurassic", calculate_years_ago=true. Let's call that.

2) Date of signing of Magna Carta: historically signed on June 15, 1215. Calculate years ago from 2026: that's 811 years ago (if counting inclusive?). Actually 2026 - 1215 = 811. If it's before June 15, 2026, still 810 years plus days. We'll just state approx 811 years ago.

Use history_get_event_date with event_name="Magna Carta signing".

Let's do calls.
